newsitem.title: FRANCE: Senegal reaches debt deal with London Club.
newsitem.headline: Senegal reaches debt deal with London Club.

text.p: The London club of bank creditors signed on Wednesday an external commercial debt reduction plan with Senegal, Banque Nationale de Paris (BNP) said.
The plan covers Senegal's commercial debt of $118 million, including $75 million of principal.

The plan provides for a cash buy-back of the principal at 16 percent with relinquishment of related interest. Alternatively there can be an exchange for non-interest bearing long-term payment instruments issued at par -- secured by zero-coupon U.S. Treasury bonds with a maturity close to 28 years -- which can be used as a means of payment in various debt conversion programmes, BNP said.

The deal becomes effective on December 23 and is the needed keystone in restoring the international financial community's confidence in Senegal and providing incentives to foreign investors, the bank said.
The deal was signed by Senegalese Finance Minister Papa Ousmane Sacko and was the result of negotiations lasting several months, BNP said.
The talks were held between Senegalese authorities and a steering committee headed by Thierry Desjardins of BNP with Citibank, Credit Lyonnais and Societe Generale as members.
